about: Threat-hunting and post-crisis DFIR tooling (doc 127). SecuRAX does not ship, bundle or re-host any third-party forensic binary: the law of these tools forbids it. Instead this is a manifest — each tool is declared with its official source, a pinned SHA-256, its licence and whether it may be redistributed at all, and is FETCHED on first use into a private, git-ignored cache (vault/hunt-tools/), or pulled from your own internal mirror. Tools whose licence forbids redistribution are 'gated': they are listed here for completeness but stay disabled until a human accepts their EULA (./securax hunt tools accept <id>), which is recorded to the audit chain. Velociraptor is the engine (Apache-2.0): it runs both as a fleet server+clients at mass scale and as a single self-contained OFFLINE COLLECTOR with no server — the minimal mode for a DevSecOps pipeline or a lone suspect host. Velociraptor's built-in Windows.KapeFiles.Targets artifact is generated from the OPEN-SOURCE KapeFiles project, not the Kroll KAPE binary, so KAPE-style triage carries no Kroll licensing exposure. The manifest is data; add your own tools, mirror URLs and pins.
mirror_note: Set SECURAX_HUNT_MIRROR to a base URL of your own internal registry (Nexus/Artifactory/S3). When set, every tool is fetched from <mirror>/<id>/<file> instead of the official source — no endpoint egress to vendor sites — and the pinned SHA-256 is still verified. Mass deployment should always use an internal mirror.

tools.name: Velociraptor
tools.role: The engine: endpoint monitoring, collection and hunting — fleet server+clients at scale, or a self-contained offline collector for minimal/pipeline mode.
tools.pin_note: Version-pinned per environment in your deploy config; set the release asset's SHA-256 here or in your mirror. CI never downloads it.

tools.name: System Informer
tools.role: Live process, handle, service and driver inspection (the successor to Process Hacker) — triage of a running suspect host.
tools.pin_note: MIT — redistributable with notice; still fetched+pinned so every node runs the same verified build.

tools.name: KapeFiles targets (open source, via Velociraptor)
tools.role: KAPE-style triage collection (the .tkape target definitions) reimplemented in Velociraptor's Windows.KapeFiles.Targets artifact — ships INSIDE Velociraptor, no separate binary.

tools.name: KAPE (Kroll Artifact Parser and Extractor)
tools.role: Kroll's triage collector+parser. Not needed for triage collection — Velociraptor's Windows.KapeFiles.Targets covers it without the binary. Listed for teams with an internal-use or Enterprise right who want the native tool.
tools.licence_note: Free for INTERNAL company use; commercial / third-party-network / paid-engagement use requires a KAPE Enterprise Licence. Licensed-not-sold, non-transferable — may not be redistributed. Confirm your right before enabling.

tools.name: FTK Imager
tools.role: Forensic disk/volume imaging and the quick capture of volatile memory, with hashing for admissibility.
tools.licence_note: Free to use; the EULA prohibits sharing the binary with third parties not bound by it — do not re-host. Fetch from the vendor on each node.

tools.name: Autoruns / autorunsc (Sysinternals)
tools.role: Enumerate every autostart/persistence location. Velociraptor has native persistence artifacts that do NOT need this binary; enable autorunsc only if you want its exact output.
tools.licence_note: Free; redistribution restricted. The no-bundle path is the official live.sysinternals.com share. Pin the exact EULA clause when enabling.

tools.name: Resource Hacker
tools.role: Inspect/extract resources from a suspect PE (icons, manifests, embedded payloads) during malware triage.
tools.licence_note: Freeware, but the author's terms forbid distributing it via any website or media without prior written approval. Fetch from angusj.com only; never bundle or mirror without that approval.
